gaps.construct: _class=HTTPMessage: a class object passed in so the parser constructs a caller-chosen Message subclass
gaps.description: No class values, no type parameters on operations (only on types, as in `Queue of T`), and no interface/subtyping to say 'some subclass of Message'. The parameter had to be dropped and the result fixed to HTTPMessage.

gaps.construct: keyword argument with a default value (_class=HTTPMessage)
gaps.description: No defaults or keyword arguments; normally one would add a second operation or make it required, but here the value itself is inexpressible.
The doc has Bytes and Text but no named encodings or decode operation; the phrase `decode ... as iso_8859_1` is invented.
No join for Bytes lists; declared a helper.

gaps.construct: email.parser.Parser(...).parsestr(...) constructing a parser object and calling a method
gaps.description: No constructors or methods; collapsed into one operation, which is fine here because the object is used once.

notes: The body is three clean lines; the cost is entirely in the headers of helpers that Python takes for granted (join, decode, parse) and in allocation becoming an explicit capability. The docstring's reasoning (why bytes, not a TextIOWrapper) has no natural home other than `note` lines; a `because` on the operation would fit if it were allowed there.
